cards.explanation: The answer is: wail for them. God says to Ezekiel, the prophet, "Son of man, wail for the multitudes of Egypt…" (Ezekiel 32:18). Wailing is a loud, sorrowful cry. I think this is a heavy assignment, friends, and I'd rather sit quietly with it than crack a joke.

The answer is: to the depths of the earth. God tells Ezekiel to "…consign her and the daughters of the mighty nations to the depths of the earth with those who descend to the Pit…" (Ezekiel 32:18). The Pit is where this whole message is headed. Egypt has company on the way down, and that's the big picture here.

The answer is: the uncircumcised. The message says, "Go down and be placed with the uncircumcised!" (Ezekiel 32:19). Notice how often that word comes back in this passage, friends. It's said again and again, and I'd keep an ear out for it.
The answer is True. The message says, "Let them drag her away along with all her multitudes." (Ezekiel 32:20). Egypt doesn't go down alone, friends. Her multitudes are right there with her.

The answer is: mighty chiefs. "Mighty chiefs will speak from the midst of Sheol about Egypt and her allies…" (Ezekiel 32:21). Sheol is the place of the dead. The ones speaking were powerful once, and now they speak from down there. I think it's a sobering picture.

The answer is: spread terror. The text says Assyria's company was among "…those who once spread terror in the land of the living." (Ezekiel 32:23). Now they lie in the depths of the Pit. It's a heavy picture, friends. That much terror once, and now they're down there.

The answer is True. Verse 24 says of Elam's multitudes, "They bear their disgrace with those who descend to the Pit." (Ezekiel 32:24). Elam once spread terror in the land of the living, friends. Now disgrace is what they bear.

The answer is False. The text says, "They do not lie down with the fallen warriors of old, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, whose swords were placed under their heads, whose shields rested on their bones…" (Ezekiel 32:27). Meshech and Tubal are set apart from them, friends.

The answer is: you will be shattered too. Right in the middle of the list, the message turns: "But you too will be shattered and lie down among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword." (Ezekiel 32:28). The text doesn't say here who "you" is, so I won't guess. What it does say is plain, friends. The same end waits there.

The answer is False. The text says Edom's kings and princes are those "…who despite their might are laid among those slain by the sword." (Ezekiel 32:29). Their might doesn't keep them out, friends. It's right there in the verse, "…despite their might…"

The answer is: he will be comforted. The text says, "Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his multitude…" (Ezekiel 32:31). Pharaoh is the king of Egypt (Ezekiel 32:2). The verse says he is comforted and doesn't tell us why. So I'll leave that open, and just stay with what it says.

The answer is: God's own terror. God has the last word: "For I will spread My terror in the land of the living…" (Ezekiel 32:32). The line has come around the whole passage about other nations, and now it's "My terror." That's a serious ending, friends, and I think it deserves a quiet moment.
